title: External frozen-image study evaluates AI colorectal-polyp characterization
summary: An external study tested a ResNet152-based colorectal-polyp characterization system on 115 images from 66 patients, using histology as the reference. For diminutive polyps, reported negative predictive values were 80% with white light and 90.9% with image enhancement, with wide confidence intervals; surveillance-interval agreement exceeded 90%. Images came from colonoscopy videos but assessment used frozen images. Real-time procedural benefit, safety of avoiding histology and broader clinical performance were not established.
organization: Portsmouth Hospitals NHS Trust; NEC Corporation

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; PMC full article.

evidence.tested: External 66-patient frozen-image diagnostic evaluation against polyp histology and endoscopist interpretation.
evidence.unknown: Real-time colonoscopy performance, safe pathology omission and generalizability remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: ResNet152 trained on 55,890 histologically labelled images from 11,068 lesions; distinct external clinical image evaluation. Frozen-image histology classification, not demonstrated real-time procedure outcomes.
